name: Aedvectis
body:
Aedvectis
CR 7

This grotesque creature has black, multifaceted eyes and a thin, 6-inch-long nose, under which you can see a bloodied maw of needle-like teeth. Even still, it wears a powdered wig, a stylish outfit fit for a noble court and handles a blade with practiced grace.

XP 3,200
NE Medium monstrous humanoid
Init +4; Senses darkvision 90 ft., scent; Perception +13; Aura mental haze (20 ft., DC 17)

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 15, flat-footed 16 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +6 natural)
hp 76 (9d10+27)
Fort +6, Ref +10, Will +7

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee +1 rapier +15/+10 (1d6+3/15-20 plus bleed) and bite +8 (1d8+1 plus bleed, disease and grab) or bite +13 (1d8+3 plus bleed, disease and grab)
Special Attacks bleed (2d4), blood drain (1d2 Constitution), draw blood
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 9th; concentration +12)

At will—alter self, bleed (DC 13), blood biography (DC 15), disguise self (DC 14)
3/day—charm person (DC 14), modify memory (DC 17)

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 19, Con 17, Int 13, Wis 12, Cha 16
Base Atk +9; CMB +11 (+15 grapple); CMD 26
Feats Deceitful, Dodge, Improved Critical (rapier), Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (rapier) Skills Bluff +22, Diplomacy +12, Disguise +22, Intimidate +8, Knowledge (nobility) +4, Perception +13, Sense Motive +4, Stealth +10; Racial Modifiers +8 Bluff, +8 Diplomacy, +8 Disguise
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Disease (Ex)

Mindmelt: Bite—injury; save Fortitude DC 17; onset 1 hour; frequency 1 day; effect 1d3 Wisdom Damage, see below; cure 2 consecutive saves.

The victim of the disease is highly suggestible. Treat any request as though delivered by suggestion (Will DC 17 negates). The save DCs are Constitution-based.

Draw Blood (Ex)

An aedvectis is extraordinarily skilled at drawing blood from his opponents. It can inflict bleed damage with any natural or manufactured slashing or piercing weapons.

Mental Haze (Ex)

An aedvectis secretes a pheromone-like substance which rapidly lowers alertness and increases the mental susceptibility of creatures around it. This substance is odorless and colorless, and thus undetectable by normal senses. Creatures in the aura must succeed at a DC 17 Will save each round or take a -1 penalty on Wisdom checks, Wisdom-based skill checks and Will saves. These penalties stack up to -10 and persist as long as the creature remains in the aura. Once the creature exits the aura’s radius, the penalties lessen by 1 each round until completely gone. The penalties don’t stack with those from the mind fog spell or similar effects. This is a mind-affecting poison effect. Aedvecti are immune to the mental haze aura.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or court (3-6 aedvecti)
Treasure standard (+1 rapier, noble outfit, other treasure)

Aedvecti are not vampires, although one unenlightened in the minutiae of hemovore differentiation would be excused for such a misconception. The major difference is, of course, their genesis. Aedvecti are not undead, but terrifying and monstrous living beings, to whom an average child of the night cannot hold a candle to in the fields of ghastliness, grotesque and debauchery. These creatures highly resemble humans, especially from the neck down. It is their faces that make the terrifying difference, merging features of a human, a mosquito and some other vague, bloodthirsty beast. Their large, dark, multifaceted eyes afford them darkvision superior to even most other creatures of the night. Their jaws are packed with needle-like teeth that can easily puncture even thick hide to draw blood. Their nose is perhaps their most distinguishing feature, being long and pointy, reminiscent of a mosquito. In contrast to the proboscis found in those insects, a nose of an aedvectis doesn’t have any function besides olfactory, but can easily rival that of a prize bloodhound in its ability to scent. While aedvecti are carnivores and can indeed eat meat, they prefer drinking blood, going as far as to keep their favorite-tasting producers as slaves and bottle especially exquisite samples as other races might keep an expensive vintage. Aedvecti are parasites through and through, rarely forming communities of their own, but rather injecting themselves into humanoid societies, especially aristocracy or other higher-class groups. They are highly adept at masquerading as frivolous nobles and many of them become so ingrained in their roles that they actually live out their lives as a new addition to the local elite. Still, their natural charm and innate ability to lie would be all for nothing if not for their inherent magic. The first and greatest use of these abilities is, of course, that allowing them to alter their appearance to fit into the race they plan to infiltrate. While they can transform entirely for longer and more risky operations, they prefer to only cloud themselves with illusions bolstered by their impressive skill at physically masking their appearance when they feel confident or need the abilities of their original form for the task at hand. Other magical abilities in their arsenal allow them to bend people to their will or erase critical memories from the minds of their targets, which they use liberally.

While an average aedvectis has a nasty bite and is rarely a slouch at fencing, their greatest weapon is their power of manipulation, enhanced by two potent tools – the substance they secrete into the air and the disease their bite carries. It is through them that aedvecti can insert themselves into established societies, infiltrating and even taking control over them in merely days. The substance they fill the air with quickly lowers awareness and dissolves the will of all who breathe it, allowing an aedvectis to charm and deceive with impunity. Then, the creature starts to pick out especially vulnerable targets, drinking their blood but leaving them alive and clueless as to what happened, but unwittingly infected with a frightful disease. While not deadly, this pathogen erodes the mind of its host, making it even easier for the aedvectis to exert control over its victim. The disease also greatly lowers the inhibitions of the person, making them extremely susceptible to even the wildest suggestions, which moves an aedvecti ever closer to its goals.

For most of those bloodsuckers, these goals don’t end at dining at their victims. Instead, they go much further than that. An aedvectis continues infecting more people, quickly making its whole social circle its unsuspecting slaves. It rarely kills, most often to keep its activities quiet or when it highly bores of a particular person, preferring to instead keep a whole menagerie of noble livestock to puppeteer at its whim. Established aedvecti often arrange for parties and banquets, deftly draining the pockets of its newfound friends, while simultaneously pushing them to ever greater heights of debauchery and depravity. Indeed, aedvecti revel in indecency, often steering the groups they control into its darkest depths. No line is too far for aedvecti and they are elated to herd their noble slaves into breaking all taboos, be they of sexual nature, related to torture and murder or blasphemy against the gods. While the greatest fun for most aedvecti lays in watching their thralls wallow in their shattered morality, most of them opt to join the games themselves, participating in boundary-breaking orgies and inventing ways of entertainment that could make a grizzled, seasoned paladin staggered with disgust. While some aedvecti keep a low profile, with their circle tightly controlled, most expand it ad infinitum, drawing in ever more people whom they can wrap around their finger and drain both their purses and veins dry. Those aedvecti always eventually have to relocate. In time, sources of coin and entertainiment start to dry up, and that forces the irritated aedvectis to either feast, tie up loose ends and vanish, or push its mind-addled slaves into ever riskier avenues of income. Those that refuse to let their empire crumble or get too invested in the fun and neglect the secrecy of their activities may quickly face retribution, as an active aedvectis is a great enemy to all, be it the lord of the land, local churches or even intrepid adventurers. Aedvecti are not territorial, but most often work alone, preferring to do things their own way and keep the spoils. Established aedvecti that know of others in the vicinity may invite each other to their debauched parties to show off their goods and outdo each other in the vileness and debauchery of their revels or the taste of their bloodslaves. It is rumored that there are aedvecti more bestial and dangerous than the ones most known to scholars. Sources are conflicted as to their origin, with some saying they form from aedvecti that cross a certain threshold of blood drinking or profligacy. Others believe they form when an aedvectis would be infected with mosquito entothropy, bringing them closer to their alleged predecessors. Others still think those tales a great load of nonsense and a horror story perpetuated to keep the aristocracy ever more sober and vigilant for fear of falling victim to such monsters. But who’s to say if those so-called greater aedvecti truly exist, forming expansive courts ruled by terrible and beautiful queens, steering entire kingdoms into a downward spiral of corruption?
